bear.text: A news report dated August 2026 states revenue rose to 1,428 crore rupees, while the company's official release reports 1,248 crore rupees for the same quarter.
The CFO stated that receivable days increased from 78 to 96 over the last year, mainly due to two large state utility customers.
The company disclosed in September 2026 that it received a GST demand order for 46.3 crore rupees related to input tax credits claimed for FY2020-21 and FY2021-22.
EBITDA margin contracted by 170 basis points to 11.2% in Q1 FY27, which management attributes mostly to rising copper prices.

bull.text: The company's order book stood at 3,900 crore rupees as of June 2026, up from 3,150 crore rupees a year earlier.
Exports contributed 21% of revenue in Q1 FY27, an increase from 16% in the same quarter of the previous year.
Management expects the new Bharuch plant to begin commercial production in Q3 FY27 and contribute to results from the second half of the year.
The share of promoter holdings pledged to lenders decreased to 4.1% in June 2026, down from 11.5% in June 2025.

open_questions.text: The company's official release reports Q1 FY27 revenue of 1,248 crore rupees, while a news article reports 1,428 crore rupees. What explains this discrepancy in the reported figures?
The company states it intends to appeal a 46.3 crore rupee GST demand order. What is the expected timeline and outcome of this legal process?
Management notes that price-variation clauses in contracts reset with a lag of one to two quarters. How will this lag affect margins in the upcoming quarters?

snapshot.text: Sarvottam Cables Ltd is a manufacturer of power cables, wires and conductors listed on the NSE.
For the quarter ended June 2026, the company reported revenue from operations of 1,248 crore rupees and profit after tax of 82 crore rupees.
As of June 2026, promoters and the promoter group held 58.2% of the company's shares.
EBITDA for the quarter ended June 2026 was 140 crore rupees, representing an 11.2% margin.
